title: One of eight heating setpoints, chosen with three binaries

blocks.text: A district heating network runs its supply water at one of a few fixed temperature setpoints; the boiler controls cannot hold anything in between. For each setpoint the operator knows the pumping power the network then needs. They are given as two lists, `temps` (°C) and `powers` (kW), with `temps[i]` and `powers[i]` belonging together:

The model in `setpoints.py` has a continuous `temp` and a continuous `power`. Write `add_setpoint(model, temp, power, temps, powers)` so that the model allows exactly the pairs `(temp, power)` that are one of the listed setpoints: no blend of two setpoints, and no setpoint's temperature with another's power. The network's full model already has hundreds of binaries, so use **at most $`\lceil \log_2 n \rceil`$ binary variables** for $`n`$ setpoints: three for eight. Add whatever continuous variables you need.
With $`i = 0, \dots, n - 1`$ the setpoints, $`T_i`$ and $`P_i`$ their temperature and power, the model so far is
This is not a curve: no two setpoints may be mixed, not even neighbours. Think about what that changes in the logarithmic form's rows, and whether the order of the codes still matters.

The tests fix the temperature and the power and ask the solver whether the model accepts the pair; one test also counts the model's integer variables. Any correct formulation within the binary limit passes. About ten lines.

from __future__ import annotations

import math

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


def add_setpoint(model: mathopt.Model, temp: mathopt.Variable, power: mathopt.Variable,
                 temps: list[float], powers: list[float]) -> None:
    """(temp, power) is one of the listed setpoints, with at most ceil(log2 n) binaries."""
    n = len(temps)
    share = [model.add_variable(lb=0, ub=1, name=f"share_{i}") for i in range(n)]
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(share) == 1, name="one_setpoint")
    model.add_linear_constraint(temp == sum(t * w for t, w in zip(temps, share)), name="temp")
    model.add_linear_constraint(power == sum(p * w for p, w in zip(powers, share)), name="power")
    for b in range(max(1, math.ceil(math.log2(n)))):
        bit = model.add_binary_variable(name=f"bit_{b}")              # setpoint i has code i
        model.add_linear_constraint(sum(w for i, w in enumerate(share) if i >> b & 1) <= bit, name=f"set_{b}")
        model.add_linear_constraint(sum(w for i, w in enumerate(share) if not i >> b & 1) <= 1 - bit,
                                    name=f"clear_{b}")


def build(temps: list[float], powers: list[float]) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, mathopt.Variable, mathopt.Variable]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="setpoints")
    temp = model.add_variable(lb=-1e6, ub=1e6, name="temp")
    power = model.add_variable(lb=-1e6, ub=1e6, name="power")
    add_setpoint(model, temp, power, temps, powers)
    return model, temp, power


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model, temp, power = build([70, 75, 80, 85], [420, 360, 310, 300])
    print(sum(v.integer for v in model.variables()), "integer variables")

cases.says: each listed temperature with its own pump power is allowed, and a listed temperature with a power no setpoint near it needs is refused
eight setpoints use at most three binaries and still refuse an unlisted pair, and three setpoints use at most two
the halfway point between two neighbouring setpoints, temperature and power both averaged, is refused
